record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Given a set of semiclassical operators that verify conditio ns 1 and 2 above, can one detect the independence axiom 3 in a purely spe ctral way? More precisely, can one tell from asymptotics of joint eigenvalues or eigenfunctions of (P1,..., Pn) that the principal symbols are almost everywhere independent? A great achievement of microlocal analysis of pseudo-differential o perators is the formulation of com- plete Bohr-Sommerfeld rules to any order. Given a quantum integrable system, these rules are, in fact, some kind of integrality conditions (or cohomological conditions), de pending on a parameter E ∈ Rn, that are satisfied if and only if E is a joint eigenvalue of the system, modulo an arbitrarily small error of size O(hbar∞ ). Historically (both in physics and mathematics), these rules have bee n written for regular Lagrangian tori, i.e., E should stay in a small ball of regular values of the classical moment ma p. More recently, non-trivial extensions to some singular situations have been found, see [50, 229, 228]. In order to treat even more physical examples, and to appeal to t he geometry community, it is impor- tant to extend these rules to Berezin-Toeplitz quantisation on com pact K ahler manifolds. This was done recently for regular tori [48], and for one degree of freedom systems with Morse singularities, see [147, 146]. It should be possible to treat the focus-focus case as well, along the lines of [227].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and let $P_1(\hbar), \dots, P_n(\hbar)$ be a family of self-adjoint semiclassical $\hbar$-pseudodifferential operators on $M$ (or on a quantizable Kähler manifold via Berezin–Toeplitz quantization) depending on a small parameter $\hbar \in (0,\hbar_0]$. Assume that:

1. The operators pairwise commute: $[P_i(\hbar), P_j(\hbar)] = 0$ for all $i,j$.
2. Each $P_i$ admits a principal symbol $p_i \in C^\infty(M;\mathbb{R})$, and the joint principal symbol map $F = (p_1, \dots, p_n) : M 	o \mathbb{R}^n$ is proper on each level (so the joint spectrum is discrete).

A classical integrability condition further requires:

3. The functions $p_1, \dots, p_n$ are almost everywhere independent, i.e.\ $dp_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge dp_n 
eq 0$ on a dense open subset of $M$.

The joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(P_1(\hbar), \dots, P_n(\hbar))$ is the set of $E = (E_1,\dots,E_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that there exists a nonzero common eigenvector $\psi$ with $P_i(\hbar)\psi = E_i \psi$ for all $i$.

Question: Suppose only conditions (1) and (2) are known. Is there a purely spectral criterion — formulated through the asymptotic behavior, as $\hbar 	o 0^+$, of the joint eigenvalues $E(\hbar)$ and/or the joint eigenfunctions of $(P_1(\hbar),\dots,P_n(\hbar))$ — that is equivalent to condition (3) (almost-everywhere independence of the principal symbols)?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific spectral-detection problem for the classical independence axiom in semiclassical quantum integrable systems was located. The problem is listed as an open problem attributed to S. Vũ Ngọc and no subsequent solution appears in available sources.
